title: Add Private minimum pack: versioned Grafana dashboard bundle (runtime + control plane + infra)
author: Sergio Costa
release_notes: Private installs: adds initial, versioned Grafana dashboard bundle for the Private Observability Minimum Pack (runtime + control plane + infra). Shipped as artifacts only; wiring via Helm/installer follows in subsequent PRs.
body: Summary: This PR adds the first versioned Grafana dashboard bundle for the Private Observability Minimum Pack. The dashboards are designed to be shipped as immutable artifacts (checked into this repo) and later installed via `redwood-helm-charts`/`redwood-private-installer` (follow-ups). Scope: 1) Runtime overview dashboard focused on golden signals + inference-specific panels (token throughput, batching, KV cache, GPU utilization). 2) Control plane health dashboard (gateway/auth/policy/config services) with standard service golden signals and dependency panels (DB/redis if present). 3) Infra dashboard for customer cluster basics required to triage most common Private incidents (node pressure, PVC pressure, pod restart loops, scrape status). Design notes / constraints: - Private environments require bounded label cardinality; dashboards avoid templating on high-cardinality labels like raw `route`, `tenant_id`, `request_id`. Where filtering is useful, panels use a small set of safe dimensions (`namespace`, `service`, `cluster`, `instance`), and model/route usage is represented via top-k panels based on recording rules (to be introduced in ENG-19144/PR-18356). - Dashboards are versioned under `dashboards/private/minimum-pack/v1.0.0/` and include stable UIDs prefixed with `rw-private-` to ensure upgrades don’t create duplicates. - Panels include conservative defaults (5m/1h ranges) and annotate ‘expected exporters’ (kube-state-metrics, node-exporter, NVIDIA DCGM exporter) but do not hard-depend on optional exporters (panels degrade gracefully when metrics are missing). What’s included (v1.0.0): - `Runtime / Overview (Private)` (UID: `rw-private-runtime-overview`) - `Control Plane / Health (Private)` (UID: `rw-private-control-plane-health`) - `Private / Cluster Infra` (UID: `rw-private-cluster-infra`) - `Private / Prometheus Scrape Health` (UID: `rw-private-prom-scrape-health`) (small helper dashboard to debug ‘empty panels’ issues) Implementation details: - Adds a bundle manifest (`dashboards/private/minimum-pack/bundle.yaml`) that enumerates dashboards, UIDs, and target folder names for the installer. - Adds lightweight validation tooling in CI (`make dashboards-validate`) to ensure exported JSON is stable, has a UID, and does not embed org-specific datasource IDs. - Standardizes dashboard tags: `redwood`, `private`, `minimum-pack`, and component tag (e.g. `runtime`, `control-plane`, `infra`). Testing: - Ran `make dashboards-validate` locally. - Imported into Grafana 10.4 with a local Prometheus, verified template variables resolve and panels render with a simulated dataset. - Verified dashboards import with no ‘Datasource not found’ errors by using named datasource `Prometheus` and `Loki` placeholders (installer will map). Follow-ups (not in this PR): - Wire into `redwood-helm-charts` values + installer packaging (ENG-19152 / PR-18405). - Add recording rules and alerts referenced by some panels (ENG-19144 / PR-18356). - Add on-prem offline bundle inclusion + checksums/signing (ENG-19154 / PR-18441).
commits: dashboards(private): add v1.0.0 runtime overview dashboard export
dashboards(private): add control plane health dashboard export
dashboards(private): add cluster infra + prometheus scrape health dashboards
packaging: introduce minimum-pack bundle manifest + folder mapping
ci: add dashboard validation script and make target
docs: note UID/tag conventions for private dashboard artifacts
review_conversation: Allison Grant (review): Can we confirm we’re not templating on model/route labels anywhere? Private cardinality guidance says no raw route/model variables in dashboard dropdowns. Sergio Costa (author): Confirmed—no dropdown variables for route/model; I removed the initial `$model` variable and replaced with a top-k table panel. The remaining variables are namespace/service/instance only. Rafael Mendes (review): Please add a small ‘Prometheus Scrape Health’ view; Support keeps getting ‘dashboards empty’ tickets where it’s actually a scrape/auth issue. Sergio Costa (author): Added `rw-private-prom-scrape-health` dashboard with target up/down, scrape duration, sample ingestion, and relabel drops. Linked it in the bundle manifest. Chloe Martin (review): UID stability is critical; please ensure all dashboards have explicit UIDs and that exports don’t include numeric datasource IDs. Sergio Costa (author): Set explicit UIDs (`rw-private-*`) and updated validation to fail if datasource is not the named placeholder. Dylan Brooks (review): Folder naming: can we standardize on `Redwood / Private / Minimum Pack` for v1? Sergio Costa (author): Done in `bundle.yaml` with a single folder target. Ethan Park (review): Control plane dashboard should include gateway 4xx/5xx split and auth/RBAC latency panels. Sergio Costa (author): Added panels for gateway status code classes and auth middleware latency histogram (when present). Approvals: Dylan Brooks approved. Chloe Martin approved. Allison Grant approved. Rafael Mendes approved.
